title: Sheetwise flat-complex computation of the compactified etale coefficient arrow
statement:
Let $e:U\to V$ be a separated etale finite-type morphism of Noetherian schemes and choose a compactification $U\xrightarrow jW\xrightarrow rV$ [def-weil-etale-morphism] [def-weil-finite-type-morphism] [def-weil-proper-morphism] [def-weil-compactifications-refinements]. Let $A\to B$ be a unital map of finite commutative rings and let $P$ be a bounded cochain complex of flat $A$-module sheaves on $U_{\rm et}$ [def-weil-pbc-etale-sheaves]. Use ordinary module derived categories, coefficient extension $T=-\otimes_A^L B$, and exact sum extension $e_{\Sigma!}$ [def-weil-pbc-derived-categories] [lem-weil-pbc-ringed-topoi-derived-tensor-pullback] [def-weil-pbc-etale-sum-extension]. The complexes $j_!P$ and $r_*j_!P$ are flat termwise and K-flat. Each term $j_!P^n$ is $r_{*,A}$-acyclic and each $j_!(P^n\otimes_A B)$ is $r_{*,B}$-acyclic; acyclic means its higher direct images vanish. The canonical acyclic-complex identifications and sheet-component normalization identify $Rr_*j_!P$ with the complex $e_{\Sigma!}P$, also after coefficient extension [lem-asd-etale-compact-support-normalization].
Under these specified models, the coefficient map formed by the proper $B$-linear counit transpose followed by the open tensor identification is represented by the natural chain map
$$(e_{\Sigma!,A}P)\otimes_A B\longrightarrow e_{\Sigma!,B}(P\otimes_A B),\qquad (x_s)_s\otimes b\longmapsto(x_s\otimes b)_s.$$
Here each element of a direct sum has finite support; the index set of sheets may be empty. This identifies the actual counit-transpose map, not merely isomorphic endpoints, and needs no flatness of $B/A$. Flatness and K-flatness use [def-pc-flat-sheaf-modules] [def-pc-kflat-complex]. Schemes and Noetherian rings use [def-pc-scheme] [def-weil-pbc-noetherian-ring].

proof.text: The compactification has $r$ proper, hence finite type, so $W$ is Noetherian by [lem-weil-pbc-finite-type-over-noetherian]. For either finite coefficient ring $R=A,B$ and any $R$-module sheaf $M$ on $U$, apply [lem-asd-etale-compact-support-normalization] to $M[0]$. It identifies $Rr_*j_!M[0]$ with $e_{\Sigma!}M[0]$. Taking cohomology gives $R^ar_*j_!M=0$ for $a>0$ and the canonical degree-zero isomorphism $r_*j_!M\cong e_{\Sigma!}M$, with exactly the sheet components specified there. Apply this first to $M=P^n$ over $A$, then to $M=P^n\otimes_A B$ over $B$. The second application requires no flatness of that sheaf over $A$. This proves both acyclicity assertions and gives natural degreewise sheet identifications.

source.place: Tag 0GL6 (remark-Rf-lower-shriek-change-of-rings), expanded bounded-model calculation; Tag 0GKF (lemma-f-shriek-projection), pure-tensor rule.

proof.text: By [lem-coef-etale-open-tensor], $j_!$ preserves flat sheaves; thus $C=j_!P$ is bounded with flat terms. By [lem-pur-etale-sum-flat-kflat], $e_{\Sigma!}P^n$ is flat for every $n$. Transporting this property through the degree-zero isomorphism of step 1 makes every $r_*C^n$ flat. Degreewise direct image and extension by zero retain the finite interval on which $P$ is supported. Apply [lem-pc-bounded-above-flat-kflat-site] to $C$ and to $r_*C$: both are K-flat. The same lemma applies to $P$ itself. These verify all flatness and K-flatness claims without a condition on $B/A$.

source.place: Tag 0GL6 (remark-Rf-lower-shriek-change-of-rings), expanded bounded-model calculation; Tag 0GKF (lemma-f-shriek-projection), pure-tensor rule.

proof.text: Apply [lem-sp-acyclic-flat-proper-coefficient-model] to $r$ and $C=j_!P$. Properness is part of the compactification; $W,V$ are Noetherian by step 1; $A,B$ are finite; boundedness, both termwise flatness assumptions, and the two direct-image acyclicity assumptions were verified in steps 1-2. For the second acyclicity assumption use the ordinary tensor isomorphism $C\otimes_A B\cong j_!(P\otimes_A B)$ of [lem-coef-etale-open-tensor]. The cited model theorem therefore identifies the actual proper $B$-adjoint transpose $q_r(C)$ with the chain map $\pi_C:(r_*C)\otimes_A B\to r_*(C\otimes_A B)$ whose degree-$n$ adjunct is the ordinary counit tensored with $1$. Compose with $r_*$ of the open tensor isomorphism. This is precisely the coefficient map in the statement, with its specified acyclic-complex identifications.

source.place: Tag 0GL6 (remark-Rf-lower-shriek-change-of-rings), expanded bounded-model calculation; Tag 0GKF (lemma-f-shriek-projection), pure-tensor rule.

proof.text: Compute that ordinary map before passing to the derived category. For an etale test scheme $S\to V$, direct image is evaluation on $W_S=W\times_VS$ [def-weil-pbc-direct-image]. Thus the adjunct defining $\pi_C^n$ sends a local pure tensor $z\otimes b$ to the section $z\otimes r^{-1}b$ on $W_S$: the ordinary counit evaluates the pulled-back section $z$. Here $b$ is a local section of the constant ring sheaf $B_V$, so the formula also covers locally constant, rather than globally constant, coefficients. The open tensor isomorphism is the identity on $U$ and zero on its complement [lem-coef-etale-open-tensor]. Under the degree-zero normalization of [lem-asd-etale-compact-support-normalization], $z$ is sent to its sheet components $(x_s)_s$. Taking the component of $z\otimes r^{-1}b$ restricts to the same sheet and hence gives $x_s\otimes b$; tensor restriction acts on each factor. Consequently the composite of step 3 is $(x_s)_s\otimes b\mapsto(x_s\otimes b)_s$. This is a calculation on local generators: by [def-weil-pbc-etale-sum-extension], sum extension is the sheafification of a presheaf of direct sums, so its sections locally come from finite sums of sheet generators; ordinary sheaf tensor is likewise generated locally by pure tensors. The calculation is additive and balanced, since $(a x_s)\otimes b=x_s\otimes\varphi(a)b$. It therefore proves equality of the sheaf morphisms, without assuming that a test scheme globally splits into sheets.

source.place: Tag 0GL6 (remark-Rf-lower-shriek-change-of-rings), expanded bounded-model calculation; Tag 0GKF (lemma-f-shriek-projection), pure-tensor rule.

proof.text: The degreewise formula commutes with the cochain differential: both composites on a generator give $(d x_s\otimes b)_s$. Naturality of the acyclic-model theorem and of the sheet normalization identifies the endpoints with the specified complexes, also after coefficient extension [lem-sp-acyclic-flat-proper-coefficient-model, lem-asd-etale-compact-support-normalization]. Hence the equality of chain maps just computed represents the named derived map. Finite sums remain finite after tensoring; for an empty sheet index the generator calculation is the unique map $0\to0$. It also covers $P=0$, $A=B$ with the identity map, and the zero coefficient ring. No tensor step used exactness of $-\otimes_A B$: K-flatness was established on the source models instead.

Step 1: applying lem-asd-etale-compact-support-normalization (finite, hence torsion, A and B; u separated, etale, finite type, Noetherian) to M[0] gives the vanishing of the higher direct images and the degree-0 sheet identification. W is Noetherian by the finite-type lemma, since r is proper. Step 2: flatness comes from lem-coef-etale-open-tensor and lem-pur-etale-sum-flat-kflat through the degree-0 isomorphism. K-flatness comes from lem-pc-bounded-above-flat-kflat-site. Step 3: every hypothesis of lem-sp-acyclic-flat-proper-coefficient-model holds. The B-side acyclicity uses the ordinary projection formula with T=B_W. The model identifies the named transpose q_r itself, not an arbitrary isomorphism. Step 4: the generator computation z⊗b -> z⊗r^{-1}b -> (x_s⊗b)_s is correct, and local generation via sheafification is justified. Step 5: the differential carries no Koszul sign. I checked the cases of empty sheets, P=0, B=0, A=B, and non-flat Z/4->Z/2. Minor unstated point, not a fault: the derived q_{j,P} equals the ordinary isomorphism on K-flat models because j_! is fully faithful and both restrict to the identity on U.
